title: A closed-loop platform engineers enzymes with minimal human input
summary: The July 2025 Nature Communications paper reports AI-guided biofoundry engineering of two enzymes in four rounds over four weeks, testing fewer than 500 variants per enzyme. Different AtHMT variants achieved about 90-fold greater ethyl-iodide substrate preference and 16-fold ethyltransferase activity; YmPhytase activity improved 26-fold at neutral pH. The system combines ML variant selection, language-model access and automated experiments; the authors describe conditional-to-high automation.
ai_technology: Machine learning and LLM-guided variant design with biofoundry automation

evidence.tested: Enzyme activity and purified-variant kinetic measurements in two campaigns.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: supplements; broad applicability beyond two enzymes. Authors classify automation between levels 3 and 4.
evidence.ai_role: Protein models and regression selected variants; the biofoundry built and tested them.
